description: I am tackling the "Be An Earth System Trend Detective!" challenge with TERRA-PULSE, an interactive scientific analytics platform I built using NASA satellite telemetry (POWER, MERRA-2, GPM, CERES) and automated statistical tests (OLS regression & Mann-Kendall) to uncover, compare, and validate multi-decadal climate trends and regional teleconnections across Earth's systems.
summary:
TERRA-PULSE is an interactive Earth observation and statistical analytics web application designed for the "Be An Earth System Trend Detective!" challenge. Because Earth's climate is an interconnected system, a single planetary cycle—such as the El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO)—can drive opposite regional outcomes, causing severe multi-decadal drought in one region while increasing precipitation in another.

TERRA-PULSE lets students, educators, and citizen scientists explore 39 years of homogenized NASA satellite records (1985–2023) on an interactive 3D orbital globe, compare two regions side by side, and run automated statistical significance tests (OLS linear regression and Mann-Kendall p < 0.05) directly in the browser. By separating true multi-decadal signals from short-term weather variability, the platform democratizes climate data literacy without requiring coding skills.
details:
What It Does & How It Works:
TERRA-PULSE is a browser-based Earth system analytics platform that transforms 39 years of NASA satellite observations (1985–2023) into accessible, statistically validated climate investigations. Users can explore data through three core workflows:

1. Mission Overview & 3D Orbital Globe: An interactive HTML5 Canvas 3D Earth with day/night shading and regional markers highlighting real-world teleconnection dipoles, such as Montevideo/Río de la Plata (+16.9% precipitation) vs. Central Valley, Chile (−58.7% precipitation) with a cross-Andes Pearson correlation of r = −0.79.
2. 3-Step Guided Investigation Wizard: Helps learners select environments, physical variables, and time windows (comparing ~13-year short windows against 35+ year records) to see how short intervals can mask or reverse true climate trends.
3. Dual-Region Trend Lab: Compares two regions side by side with SVG time-series charts, Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) regression slopes, 95% confidence intervals, non-parametric Mann-Kendall significance tests (p < 0.05), linear 2050 trajectory indicators (explicitly noting model limitations), a Multi-Sensor Anomaly Radar, and one-click CSV export of co-located telemetry.

Benefits & Intended Impact:
By combining a no-code guided interface with rigorous statistical testing and reproducible CSV exports, TERRA-PULSE empowers students, teachers, journalists, and local communities to verify environmental trends and counter climate misinformation using authentic NASA telemetry.

Tools, Languages & Software Used:
Built with React 18, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, a custom HTML5 Canvas 3D orthographic globe, a custom TypeScript statistical engine (OLS, Mann-Kendall, Pearson correlation), and the NASA Langley Research Center (LaRC) POWER API, deployed on Vercel with source code hosted on GitHub.

Creativity & Key Considerations:
Instead of displaying isolated single-location charts, TERRA-PULSE introduces a dual-region "Teleconnection Dipole Meter" that pairs opposing climatic outcomes side by side, ensuring both scientific rigor (non-parametric testing and explicit projection caveats) and intuitive visual storytelling.
